title: Gemma 4 Deep Dive — Cassidy Hardin, Researcher, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A DeepMind researcher walks through Gemma 4's architecture: dense 31B and first MoE 26B (128 experts, 8 active, 3.9B active params), plus on-device E2B/E4B using per-layer embeddings stored in flash memory, interleaved local/global attention with grouped-query attention, and variable-resolution/soft-token-budget vision.

takeaways.technique: Small open-weight models as cheap tier for routine agent work
takeaways.what_they_do: Releases Apache 2.0 small models (E2B/E4B on-device, 26B MoE with only 3.9B active params) positioned as capable enough for agentic/coding tasks at low serving cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: This model has been adapted to have incredible performance while only requiring 3.9 billion active parameters.
takeaways.numbers: 26B MoE, 128 experts, 8 active, 3.9B active params; 31B dense ranked top-6 open-source on LM Arena

takeaways.what_they_do: Lets callers pick resolution and a soft-token budget per image (five levels), so image tokens are a deliberate cost knob rather than fixed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you now have a choice when you're running a Gemma model to select the resolution and the soft token budget that you want to allocate for images
takeaways.numbers: 5 resolutions; token budget 280 ≈ 2,520 patches; 3x3 patch pooling to 1 soft token

takeaways.technique: Offload rarely-used weights to flash instead of VRAM
takeaways.what_they_do: Stores per-layer embedding tables in flash memory rather than VRAM, trading a cheap lookup for scarce fast memory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we store our PLE, our per-layer embedding table, in flash memory as opposed to VRAM
takeaways.numbers: PLE embedding dim 256 vs full model; 35/42 layers
